questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

The course (has been) a success with more than a thousand students joining it.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'No improvement'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **In the given sentence,** 'has' is used for the subject 'course' which is a singular noun. 'been' is the third form of the verb 'be'.
 
• 'With more than a thousand students joining it' is a phrase that tells that the action is still continuing and in-process. This action was started in the past hence, we need to use the perfect tense which is correctly used in the sentence.

**So the correct sentence is-** *The course has been a success with more than a thousand students joining it.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

That game (were interrupted) by the rains; it resumed an hour after, when the rains stopped.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'was interrupted'**

**__Key Points__**

 
• The given bracketed part is to be replaced with 'was interrupted' because the subject of the sentence is 'game' which is a singular noun hence use the singular verb with it.
 
• We cannot use the present tense here, because the subordinate clause 'when the rains stopped' is in the past tense. Hence use the past tense in the main clause too.

**So the correct sentence is-** *That game was interrupted by the rains; it resumed an hour after, when the rains stopped*.

**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

• The following things to be remembered while changing the active voice into the passive voice-
 
 
• **Firstly,** check the tense of the sentence because it is not going to be changed in the passive voice.
 
• **Secondly,** check whether the sentence has an object in it. If it doesn't then go for the infinitive phrase.
 
• The structure of the passive voice is- Subject + Verb (be) + V₃ (past participle) + by + Object.
 
 
 
• **So according to the steps, the correct passive voice of the given sentence is-** *it will be conquered by me. *

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Along with Plato, Aristotle is considered the father of Western (1)/Philosophy, which from his teachings inherited almost its entire (2)/ lexicon, including problems and methods of inquiry. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2' **i.e**. '2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The relative clause in part 2, **"which from his teachings inherited almost its entire lexicon,"** contains an error in the placement of phrases.
 
• The phrase **"from his teachings" **is misplaced, making the sentence awkward and difficult to understand.
 
• **"Its**" refers to **"Western Philosophy," **and indicates that the lexicon of Western Philosophy is almost entirely derived from Aristotle's teachings.
 
• The correct structure is *"which inherited almost its entire lexicon from his teachings" *to maintain clarity and grammatical correctness.

Therefore, the correct answer is:** 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **Along with Plato, Aristotle is considered the father of Western

 
 
• This part of the sentence is correct, setting the context without any grammatical errors.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** lexicon, including problems and methods of inquiry.
 
 
• This part is also correct, as it properly lists the components included in the lexicon that Western Philosophy inherited.

questions.question: In the following question, four groups of three numbers are given. In each group the second and third number are related to the first number by a Logic/Rule/Relation. Three are similar on basis of same Logic/Rule/Relation. Select the odd one out from the given alternatives.
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:-

**(First number)² = Second number**

**First number × (First number)² = Third number**

1) In (2, 4, 8)

(2)² = 4

2 × (2)² = 2 × 4 = 8

2) In (3, 9, 27)

(3)² = 9

3 × (3)² = 3 × 9 = 27

3) In (4, 16, 32)

(4)² = 16

4 × (4)² = 4 × 16 = 64 not 32

4) In (5, 25, 125)

(5)² = 25

5 × (5)² = 5 × 25 = 125

As can be seen clearly from the above that (4, 16, 32) doesn't follow the logic and is the odd one out from the given alternatives.

Hence, the correct answer is **"(4, 16, 32)".**

questions.question: What is the x-intercept of line joining (4, 2) and (6, 3)?
questions.solution:

Let X₁ = 4, X₂ = 6, Y₁ = 2 & Y₂ = 3

Equation of line

⇒ (Y - Y₁) = (Y₂ - Y₁)/(X₂ - X₁₎) × (X - X₁)

⇒ (Y - 2) = (3 - 2) /(6 - 4) × (X - 4)

⇒ 2Y - 4 = X - 4

⇒ X - 2Y = 0

⇒ X = 2Y

At X intercept, Y = 0

**∴ X = 0**

questions.question: The lengths of the two diagonals of a rhombus are 7 cm and 24 cm. Find the length of its perimeter (in cm).
questions.solution:
Calculation:

The lengths of the first diagonal (d₁) = 7

The length of the second diagonal (d₂) = 24 cm

⇒ a² = (d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)² (as diagonals of rhombus bisect at 90°)

⇒ a² = (7/2)² + (24/2)²

⇒ a² = 49/4 + 144

⇒ a² = √(625/4)

⇒ a = 25/2

**∴ Perimeter of rhombus = 4 × a = 4 × 25/2 = 50 cm**

questions.question: If the perimeter of a semicircle is 36 cm, then find its area (in cm²).
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Perimeter of semicircle = πr + 2r

⇒ 36 = πr + 2r

⇒ 36 = (22/7 + 2) × r

⇒ 36 = 36/7 × r

⇒ r = 7 cm

Area of semicircle = 1/2 × πr²

= 1/2 × 22/7 × 7 × 7

**= 77 cm²**

The radius of hemisphere (r) = 21 cm

Calculation:

Given, sin U = 24/25

Sin U = (Perpendicular)/hypotenuse = VW/UW = 24/25

Let VW = 24k and UW = 25k

By Pythagoras' theorem

UV² = UW² - VW²

⇒ 0.7² = 625k - 576k

⇒ 0.49 = 49k²

⇒ k² = 0.49/49 = 0.01

⇒ k = 0.1

**Thus, length of side VW = 24k = 24 × 0.1 = 2.4 cm**

• They capture their prey by putting out pseudopodia also called false feet.
 
• An example is *Amoeba.*
 
• *Amoeba* also has a contractile vacuole, it is an osmoregulatory organ.
 
• The contractile vacuole controls the intracellular water balance by expelling excess water from the body.
 
 
 
• Flagellated protozoans
 
 
• They have flagella as a locomotory organ.
 
• They can be free-living or parasitic.
 
• An example is *Trypanosoma*. It causes sleeping sickness.
 
 
 
• Ciliated protozoans
 
 
• They are aquatic and actively moving organisms because of the presence of locomotory organs called cilia.
 
• The cilia help in the movement of water along with the food inside the body cavity.
 
• An example is *Paramoecium*. It has a dimorphic nucleus.
 
• It has one small nucleus called a micronucleus and one large nucleus called a macronucleus.
 
 
 
• Sporozoans
 
 
• They have an infectious spore-like stage in their life cycle.
 
• An example is* Plasmodium*. It causes malaria in humans.

questions.question: Which among the following is respiratory pigment in human beings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Haemoglobin.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Hemoglobin molecules with the help of external chemical factors take up oxygen molecules in the lungs and then send them to the various tissues of our body.

 
• Iron is the **main constituent** of hemoglobin.
 
• The **normal level** of hemoglobin is 13 to 17 grams per deciliter in men and 12.0 to 15.5 grams per deciliter in women.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Melanin is a dark biological pigment found in skin, hair, feathers, scales, eyes, and some internal membranes.
 
• Rhodopsin is called visual purple, a pigment-containing sensory protein that converts light into an electrical signal. 
 
• **Bilirubin** is a yellowish substance in your blood. It **forms after red blood cells break down**, and it travels through your liver, gallbladder, and digestive tract before being excreted.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The biggest regulator of oxygen affinity in Hemoglobin is the oxygen itself.
 
• If in the lungs, the oxygen levels are high the Hemoglobin shows a greater affinity towards the oxygen molecules, and as it bounds to more oxygen, this property of affinity increases and vice versa.
 
• When the Oxyhemoglobin binds to the maximum capacity, it becomes saturated but its affinity towards oxygen increases whereas when this binding loose oxygen molecule the affinity decreases.
 
• This regulation activity is called Cooperativity and is an important function as it allows the maximum amount of Hemoglobin to be carried to the tissues and also allows deoxyhemoglobin which is releasing the oxygen tissue.

questions.question: China has successfully launched two Beidou-3 satellites on board of which carrier rocket?
questions.solution:
The Beidou-3M/G/I satellites represent the orbital segment of the third phase of the Chinese Beidou navigation system which uses satellites in Medium Earth Orbit and Geosynchronous Orbit and is also known as the Compass Navigation Satellite System

The Long March 3B also known as the CZ-3B and LM-3B, is a Chinese orbital carrier rocket. Introduced in 1996, it is launched from Launch Area 2 and 3 at the Xichang Satellite Launch Centre in Sichuan.

questions.question: In May 2017, the base year of All-Indian WPI (Wholesale Price Index) has been revised from 2004-05 to_________.
questions.solution:
The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) is the price of a representative basket of wholesale goods.

India has adopted new Consumer price Index to measure inflation since it considers the price at which the final consumer purchases essential consumer goods.

questions.question: From May 2017, the Real estate act has come into effect. It aims to protect the interests of _________.
questions.solution:
The Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 is an Act of the Parliament of India which seeks to protect home-buyers as well as help boost investments in the real estate industry.

The Act establishes Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA) in each state for regulation of the real estate sector and also acts as an adjudicating body for speedy dispute redressal.

questions.question: Calculate the frequency (in Hz) of a sound wave of wavelength 4m travelling with a speed of 200 m/s.
questions.solution: The hertz (symbol: Hz) is the derived unit of frequency in the International System of Units (SI) and is defined as one cycle per second. The wavelength is the spatial period of a periodic wave which is basically the distance over which the wave's shape repeats. It is thus the inverse of the spatial frequency.

questions.question: The numerical value of a physical quantity is its ________.
questions.solution:
An order of magnitude is an approximate measure of the size of a number, equal to the logarithm rounded to a whole number.

For example, the order of magnitude of 1500 is 3, because 1500 = 1.5 × 10³

questions.question: Humidity is a measure of the ________.
questions.solution:
• Humidity is the amount of water vapour present in the air. Water vapour is the gaseous state of water and is invisible to the human eye.
 
• Humidity indicates the likelihood of precipitation, dew, or fog.
